scenes.title: The San Juan Bautista sails
scenes.caption: Date Masamune had the galleon built in 45 days by Japanese shipwrights with help from the Spanish navigator Sebastián Vizcaíno's crew. She sailed from Tsukinoura in October 1613 with about 180 people: samurai, merchants and Spaniards.

scenes.title: Three months on the Pacific
scenes.caption: The crossing took about ninety days, on the great-circle route north to the westerlies and down the coast of California: the route the Manila galleons used. The ship carried Japanese and Spanish crews who had to share one deck and one language of signs.

scenes.title: Samurai in Mexico City
scenes.caption: In Mexico City the Nahua chronicler Chimalpahin noted the Japanese envoy's arrival in his diary, and that some of the samurai were baptised at the church of San Francisco. Japanese in kimono walked the streets of the viceroy's capital.

scenes.title: The fortress of San Juan de Ulúa
scenes.caption: At Veracruz the embassy waited for the fleet to Spain under the walls of San Juan de Ulúa, the island fortress guarding New Spain's one Atlantic port, where the silver of Mexico was loaded for Seville.

scenes.title: The treasure fleet at Havana
scenes.caption: The ships from Veracruz joined the treasure fleet at Havana, where the galleons gathered each summer to cross the Atlantic together under escort. The Japanese envoys saw tobacco, pineapples and a harbour full of ships.

scenes.title: Arrival at Seville
scenes.caption: Seville greeted the embassy with a procession, and Hasekura presented a letter from his lord, Date Masamune, asking for trade with New Spain. The letter is still kept in the city's archive.

scenes.title: Baptism in Madrid
scenes.caption: On 17 February 1615 Hasekura was baptised in the chapel of the Descalzas Reales convent in Madrid, with the Duke of Lerma as his godfather and King Philip III present. He took the name Felipe Francisco.

scenes.title: Before the Pope
scenes.caption: In November 1615 Hasekura was received by Pope Paul V in the Quirinal Palace and made an honorary citizen of Rome. A portrait of him painted in Rome, in a richly embroidered kimono, survives in the Borghese collection.

scenes.title: The Parián of Manila
scenes.caption: On the way home the embassy waited two years in Manila, a Spanish city whose trade lived on Chinese junks: thousands of Chinese merchants and craftsmen lived outside the walls in the Parián, and a Japanese quarter, Dilao, lay nearby.

scenes.title: Home to a closed country
scenes.caption: Hasekura came home in 1620 after seven years to find Christianity banned across Japan and his lord unable to protect converts. He died two years later; the gifts he brought back, a portrait and a rosary among them, were hidden and survived in the Date family's storehouse.
